detail: Settle the debt payoff order. Prerequisite: a debt inventory, which has been open since Jul 2026 (routine.md:51; TASKS.md:64; finance/tracker.yml:27 debts: []).

Minimum-viable inventory: one row per debt in finance/tracker.yml with creditor, minimum payment, due day, and autopay yes/no. Balance and APR are optional this round. Figures stay in tracker.yml, never in memory.

Circular gate keeps the inventory empty: tracker.yml:3 says not to enter figures until the TASKS.md inventory is complete, and TASKS.md:64 says the tracker stays empty until the inventory is done. Item open ~15 weeks with zero rows; treat as friction/avoidance, not a real constraint.

Organize the day better. Reframed from scheduling to a closed daily loop: capture what a workday produced, and decide the next day's first action in advance. Evidence: weekly rhythm has no daily slot (routine.md:15); 58 unchecked boxes in TASKS.md with no today layer; progress/ and reflections/ empty; 0 calendar: annotations in TASKS.md despite the publisher built 2026-11-06.
One line per workday in progress/work-log.md: YYYY-MM-DD | done: <what shipped> | next: <first action tomorrow>. 60 seconds at end of workday. First line's next: field must be the debt inventory row.

System-build substitutes for system-use. The calendar/Tasks publisher is built and verified as of 2026-11-06, but TASKS.md has zero calendar: annotations; progress/ and reflections/ are empty; the weekly review's work-log input is missing (routine.md:26; DASHBOARD.md:16). Planning capacity is not the constraint; capture and follow-through are.

Chose the daily one-line capture log over (a) a morning Top-3 in TASKS.md, (b) time-blocking through the existing Google Tasks publisher, (c) pruning the 58-item backlog first. Reason: capture is the missing feedback loop and the smallest step; time-blocking depends on the unused publisher. Backlog pruning is deferred, not rejected.
